title: Self Publishing on Amazon: Pros and Cons for First-Time Authors | Legenddary's SparkPrep
h1: Self-publishing on Amazon: the pros and cons for your first book
description: Is self-publishing on Amazon KDP worth it? The real pros and cons in plain English: free to start, 70% ebook royalties, the 2025 paperback royalty change, and why files get rejected.
lead: Amazon KDP is where most first-time authors start. It's free and fast, but it has rules and trade-offs nobody explains up front. Here are the honest pros and cons.
body:
The pros

  • It's free to publish. No setup fee for an ebook, paperback or hardcover. Printing is taken out of each sale, so you don't pay up front.
  • Huge reach. Your book is sold on Amazon, where many readers already shop for books.
  • Good ebook royalties. You can earn 70% on ebooks priced from $2.99 to $9.99 (KDP ebook royalties). Outside that range it's 35%.
  • Fast. Books usually go live within about 3 business days after you hit publish.
  • Print on demand. Amazon prints a copy only when someone buys it. No boxes of books in your garage.

The cons

  • Lower royalties on cheap paperbacks. Since June 10, 2025, KDP pays 60% on print books priced at $9.99 or more, but only 50% below that, minus printing (KDP paperback royalty).
  • Exclusivity if you join KDP Select. Select puts your ebook in Kindle Unlimited, but you can't sell that ebook anywhere else for 90 days at a time. It's optional.
  • Bookstores rarely stock KDP books. Most bookstores and libraries order through IngramSpark, which is why many authors use both.
  • Strict file rules. KDP checks page size, margins, bleed and picture sharpness. If one thing is off, your file is sent back and you fix it and wait again.
  • Amazon controls the store. Amazon can discount your book, and its rules can change, as the 2025 royalty change showed.

Is self-publishing on Amazon worth it?

For most first-time authors, yes. It costs nothing to start and reaches the most readers. Price your paperback at $9.99 or more if you can, to get the 60% rate. Decide on KDP Select only for your ebook, and only if you're fine selling it on Amazon alone.

The step most new authors skip

The biggest time-waster on KDP is a rejected file. The usual causes: margins too small, no bleed, blurry pictures and a cover that's the wrong size. Checking your files before you upload saves you the back-and-forth. New to all this? Start with how to self-publish a book in 7 steps.

cta.text: Amazon is free to start. A rejected file is what slows you down. SparkPrep checks your cover and pages against KDP's rules and fixes them before you upload.

faq.a: Yes. Amazon KDP charges nothing to publish an ebook, paperback or hardcover. Printing is taken out of each sale.

faq.q: How much does Amazon pay authors?
faq.a: KDP pays 70% on ebooks priced $2.99 to $9.99 and 35% otherwise. Since June 10, 2025, print books earn 60% at $9.99 or more and 50% below that, minus printing.

faq.q: What are the downsides of self-publishing on Amazon?
faq.a: Lower royalties on paperbacks under $9.99, 90-day ebook exclusivity if you join KDP Select, few bookstore orders, strict file rules that cause rejections, and Amazon controls pricing and policies.

answer.q: What are the pros and cons of self-publishing on Amazon?
answer.a: Pros: it's free, fast (about 3 business days), reaches the most readers and pays 70% on ebooks priced $2.99 to $9.99. Cons: paperbacks under $9.99 earn 50% instead of 60%, KDP Select ebooks are Amazon-only for 90 days, bookstores rarely order KDP books, and strict file rules cause rejections.
